name: ablation_benchmark
description: NEEDS ONE PATH SUBSTITUTION BEFORE IT WILL RUN -- see _model_paths below. Does the DeepSets structure win GAMES, or only validation loss? Four arms as the pure-network agent against SakkirinaSolo, 400 games each: the DeepSets control, the parameter-matched flat MLP, the 22.57x-capacity flat MLP, and the parameter-matched flat MLP with canonically sorted rows. All four were trained on one split with one seed through one loop, differing only in the network. COMPLETE: 1,600/1,600 games, all clean, every loaded model hash-verified per row. Results in REPRODUCE.md section 9.
_why_games_and_not_just_val_loss: The offline ranking does not predict playing strength, so the ablation is decided by
games, not by validation loss alone.
Re-scored on the full validation split, the shipped model ranks last of the six
seed-benchmark checkpoints on every offline metric (highest loss, lowest accuracy,
lowest AUC, highest Brier) and first on win rate, at 80.25%. Seed 4 is best on
accuracy and AUC and the weakest player, at 69.25%. With six models whose offline
losses span 0.0154 this is not evidence of anticorrelation, but the offline ranking
says nothing about playing strength at these margins.
The ablation's offline gap is much larger: 0.0293 in loss to the matched arm, about
2.7x the spread across the five DeepSets seeds, at p < 1e-9 game-clustered. Whether
that carries over to games is what this config measures.
_interchangeability_was_verified: The ONNX files load unchanged in Bots/src/DeepSetsCore.cs, although three of them
are a different architecture. All four have the shipped model's signature:
output   win_probability [batch_size, 1] float32, a raw logit
The flat models pad, flatten and concatenate inside the graph, so
ValueNetworkEvaluator needs no new feature extractor.
The output scale was checked as well: a model emitting a probability would be
sigmoided twice by the bot and play like a flatter evaluator without any error. On
logits, none inside [0,1], pairwise correlation 0.88-0.93. Node counts from 1 to 128
_check_before_interpreting: Check the evaluations-per-turn column; the flat arms should come out lower.
python tools/aggregate_benchmark_results.py --config ablation_benchmark --out-dir $OUT_DIR
In seed_benchmark.json every row should search equally and a low row means a broken
export. Here the flat models are slower per inference, so a low row is expected.
Measured on an x86 compute node, single-threaded, 5000 real validation states
(tools/compare_onnx_models.py): DeepSets 49.0 us median, matched 60.7 us (1.24x
slower), wide 240.0 us (4.7x slower).
Expected ratios, relative to the deepsets row:
matched   0.81x to 0.94x
wide      0.20x to 0.48x
matched_sorted  at or slightly below matched (the canonical sort adds an
argsort/TopK over at most 128 rows per inference)
Observed: matched 1.04x, wide 0.40x, matched_sorted 0.92x. Wide fell in its range;
matched came out slightly above the control, so a flat arm above 1.00x is not by
itself evidence of a fallback. The bounds are the two ends of a modelling assumption.
The low end assumes a turn's time goes entirely to inference, so evaluations scale as
1/inference_time. The high end adds a fixed per-evaluation search cost (move
generation, tree bookkeeping, simulation) of about 127 us, solved from the only two
(inference us, evals/turn) points measured on the same hardware and config: the
invalid first seed run's ~700 us / ~1,430 evals and the shipped row's ~58 us / 6,401
evals (see seed_benchmark.json's _first_run_was_invalid).
So with the deepsets row near 6,400 evaluations per turn, expect roughly
5,200-6,000 for matched and 1,300-3,100 for wide.
A wide row anywhere near the deepsets row would mean the SOT_MODEL_PATH substitution
did not take and the arm fell back to GameRunner's copy of the shipped model. The
per-row hash readback (_what_the_pin_guarantees, layer 3) checks for that directly.
The arms are matched on wall clock, which is what a deployed agent gets, not on
search volume. A flat arm that loses does so on evaluation quality and evaluation
rate combined, and this config cannot separate the two. It answers 'should we have
built the flat model instead', not 'is the set structure a better evaluator'; the
latter needs SOT_TIME_SCALE on the faster side, as in equal_effort.json.
_model_paths: Every SOT_MODEL_PATH below must be edited before submitting. One substitution:
CHANGE_ME_HPCWORK -> the literal expansion of $HPCWORK on your cluster
The paths must be absolute. A relative path is resolved against two different
- the game runs with cwd=GameRunner/bin/Release/net8.0, and the bot calls
File.Exists on the same string from there.
A relative path can pass the harness and miss in the bot, which then logs the
rejection and falls back to GameRunner's copy of the shipped model. Every arm would then
$HPCWORK is not expanded: no shell runs between this file and the bot, so a literal
"$HPCWORK/..." is not found. Substitute the expanded path by hand.
An unedited config cannot run: tools/benchmark_cluster.py aborts the task with exit 1
and no result file if SOT_MODEL_PATH does not exist, which CHANGE_ME_* paths fail.
_what_the_pin_guarantees: Model pins, in three layers:
1. builtin_onnx_sha256 (absent here, so the shipped default applies) is checked
against GameRunner's own copy of the model by tools/benchmark_cluster.sh, as a
stale-build check.
2. allowed_onnx_sha256 lists the ablation models. tools/benchmark_cluster.py
hashes the file a row's SOT_MODEL_PATH names and requires it to be on that
list before the game runs.
3. After every game, the harness reads back the sha256 the bot logged in
PregamePrepare and requires it to equal that row's model hash. A mismatch, or
no such line, fails the task and writes no result.
Layers 1 and 2 are set checks on files: they confirm a task pointed at a known
model, not that the matched row ran the matched model. The likely failure is a
SOT_MODEL_PATH the bot cannot resolve, after which it falls back to GameRunner's
built-in copy and plays a complete game with the shipped model. For the deepsets
control row, which has the shipped model's architecture and speed, neither the win
rate nor evaluations per turn would show it. Layer 3 does.
The shipped model's 86e0f9a8... is not in allowed_onnx_sha256: no row here loads it,
and listing it would let a fallback to the built-in copy pass layer 2.
seed_benchmark lists it because the shipped model is one of its rows.
Every result JSON records the task's env and a 'loaded_models' block with the path,
size and sha256 each bot loaded, so a finished run can be audited row by row.
_comparability: seed_base 20260930 is used by no other config. seed = seed_base + task_id and task
ids run contiguously across matchups, so arm N plays seeds 20260930+400N onwards: a
different 400 games per arm, not paired deals.
Pairing the arms on one seed range would stop the harness telling their result files
apart by task id; seed_benchmark has the same limitation. Read differences against
the Wilson intervals the aggregator prints, not as a ranking. At 400 games per arm
that resolves about 6 points at 95% confidence; the offline gap predicts more than
that for wide and possibly less for matched.
_fourth_row_added_after_the_first_three_: flat_matched_sorted was added after rows 0-2 had run and is last, so their task-id
ranges (0-399, 400-799, 800-1199) and result files are unchanged; --array=1200-1599
runs it alone, and the aggregator reads all four. Its hash b71981086314... is on the
allowed list. All four arms are complete: 1,600/1,600 games, all clean, each game's
loaded model verified against its row's hash.
The first three rows test flat models that are not permutation-invariant, inside a
search that reshuffles hidden piles on every determinisation. On the trained models,
reshuffling one board moves flat-matched's logit by sd 0.40, 1.21x the change a real
move produces, and flips its predicted winner on 26% of states; DeepSets moves by
exactly 0. The 31-point game gap between deepsets and flat_matched therefore mixes a
worse evaluator with missing invariance. This row separates the two; sorting a set
canonically before an MLP is the standard baseline.

matchups.label: deepsets
matchups.note: The control: the paper's architecture, retrained on the same split and seed as the two flat arms so the comparison is like-for-like. 73,089 parameters, val loss 0.4290, 78.65% accuracy, sha256 4619288b... Expect roughly 6,400 evaluations per turn, in line with the shipped row of seed_benchmark.

matchups.label: flat_matched
matchups.note: Parameter-matched flat MLP, 12691->5->128->64->1, 72,549 parameters (0.99x the control). Val loss 0.4635, 76.73% accuracy, sha256 bbbccfb7... 1.24x slower per inference on x86, so expect 0.81-0.94x the control's evaluations per turn. Note 61.9% of its weights are identically zero after the export flush -- matched by parameter COUNT, not by effective capacity; see REPRODUCE.md section 9.

matchups.label: flat_wide
matchups.note: Flat MLP with 22.57x the control's capacity, 12691->128->128->64->1, 1,649,409 parameters. Val loss 0.5325, 75.83% accuracy, sha256 26c396d8... This arm exists to foreclose the objection that the matched arm was starved: it is worse than matched offline on every metric and in every prestige bucket. 4.7x slower per inference, so expect only 0.20-0.48x the control's evaluations per turn -- it is doubly penalised here, and a heavy loss is the prediction rather than a surprise.

matchups.label: flat_matched_sorted
matchups.note: Identical to flat_matched -- 12691->5->128->64->1, 72,549 parameters -- except that the node rows are put into a canonical order before flattening, INSIDE the model, so training, offline scoring and ONNX inference all share it and no C# changes. Verified permutation-invariant: reshuffling the hidden piles changes the flattened vector, and the exported graph's output, by exactly 0 (2,000 reshuffles over 250 real states), as it does for DeepSets. Compare this row against flat_matched to separate evaluator quality from the absence of permutation invariance; the difference between the two IS the cost of unsorted rows in a determinising search. Hash and expected evaluations per turn are unknown until it is trained -- the canonical sort adds an argsort/TopK over at most 128 rows per inference, which is small beside a 12,691-dim matvec but not free, so expect its evaluations per turn at or slightly below flat_matched's.
